entry.title: Ambient cubic-container problem for visibility cliques
entry.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite point set. A **visibility patch** is a subset $W\subset\Gamma(\mathbb{R})$ of a real cubic on which the relevant pairs of points are considered, and an ambient blocker for a pair from $A\cap W$ is a point of $A\setminus\Gamma$ lying in the open segment joining that pair. **Ambient cubic-container problem.** For every $k,\ell$ there are constants $\alpha>0$ and $\beta<1/(\ell-1)$ such that, if $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ has $n$ points, no $k$ collinear points, and no $\ell$ mutually visible points, then there is a real cubic $\Gamma$ and a visibility patch $W\subset\Gamma(\mathbb{R})$ for which

$$
|A\cap W|\ge \alpha n
$$

and the number of ambient blockers in $A\setminus\Gamma$ for pairs from $A\cap W$ is at most

$$
\beta |A\cap W|.
$$

This is identified as the missing ambient container theorem that could combine with the paper's cubic-container result to prove the Big-Line–Big-Clique Conjecture. It is posed as an open problem.
entry.source_name: Sohail Sarkar, “Visibility cliques, cubic containers, and dense orchard cores”, arXiv:2605.00918 (2026).
entry.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00918

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).

entry.title: Spanning-subtree probability conjecture for the complete graph
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, let $s_k(G)$ be the number of subtrees of $G$ with $k$ vertices, and define the spanning-subtree probability

$$
p(G)=\frac{s_n(G)}{\sum_{k=1}^n s_k(G)}.
$$

**Spanning-subtree probability conjecture.** For every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices,

$$
p(G)\le p(K_n).
$$

The source states that this less restrictive conjecture is an open problem and that it would support the extremality of the complete graph.

entry.title: The path and clique extremality conjecture for mean subtree order
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, and let $\mu(G)$ denote its mean subtree order. Write $P_n$ for the path and $K_n$ for the clique on $n$ vertices.

**Mean subtree order extremality conjecture.**

$$
\mu(P_n) \le \mu(G) \quad\text{with equality if and only if }G=P_n,
$$

and

$$
\mu(G) \le \mu(K_n) \quad\text{with equality if and only if }G=K_n.
$$

The minimum assertion is proved in the paper, while the maximum assertion remains open; thus the full conjecture is not resolved.

entry.title: Connected-graph contraction conjecture for mean subtree order
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph and let $e\in E(G)$. Write $G/e$ for the graph obtained by contracting $e$, and let $\mu$ denote mean subtree order.

**Connected-graph contraction conjecture.** Contracting any edge should reduce the mean subtree order by at least $\frac13$, with equality only for a path:

$$
\mu(G)-\mu(G/e)\ge\frac13,
$$

with equality if and only if $G$ is a path.
The source presents this as a proposed generalisation of the proved tree case and says that proving it would imply the path-minimum result.

entry.title: Irreducibility conjecture for reciprocal subsum numerators
entry.statement: Let $n\geq 1$, and let $\mathrm{num}(n,x)$ denote the numerator polynomial associated with sums of reciprocals of subsum polynomials over partitions of $n$. **Irreducibility conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$, the polynomial $\mathrm{num}(n,x)$ is irreducible over the integers. This is supported by numerical evidence and is posed as an open question.
entry.review_depth: Literal statement read; see per-ID narrative for actual primary-body/search depth, not full literature clearance

entry.title: Cyclotomic nondivisibility conjecture for binary-partition numerators
entry.statement:
Let $\mathcal B(n)$ be the set of binary partitions of $n$, and let $\mathrm{num}_{\mathcal B}(n,x)$ be the associated numerator polynomial. **Binary-partition nondivisibility conjecture.** For every $n\geq 2$ and every integer $i$ satisfying $2^i\leq n$, 
$$
1+x^{2^i}\nmid \mathrm{num}_{\mathcal B}(n,x).
$$
 The paper gives evidence for this conjecture, which remains open.

entry.title: Gravier–Maffray list-coloring conjecture for claw-free graphs
entry.statement:
A graph is **claw-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,3}$. Let $\chi(G)$ and $\chi_\ell(G)$ denote the chromatic and list chromatic numbers. **Gravier–Maffray's conjecture.** For every claw-free graph $G$,

$$
\chi_\ell(G)=\chi(G).
$$

This is the broad chromatic-choosability conjecture for claw-free graphs; the supplied text does not resolve it in general.
